post.description:
Upload a file to a target table.

The file is stored in S3/R2, then the Internal API creates a FileKit
asset record and Hyperframe row via AMQP RPC. This triggers the same
Chronos ingestion/extraction workflows as the UI.

Idempotent on external_id per target: re-submitting the same
external_id returns the original response with HTTP 200.

post.description:
Trigger a new processing run on an already-uploaded file.

The row's status is reset to 'uploading', which re-triggers the existing
Chronos ingestion/extraction workflow without requiring a new file upload.
The original row and any prior exports remain on the same file_id.

Split-aware: preinvoice batches are split per-company during ingestion and
the original upload row is deleted, so on a missing parent we fall back to
the split children (matching get_file_status) and reprocess each terminal
one — the response still echoes the original file_id.

Webhook: one ``file.reprocessed`` event is emitted with the parent
``file_id`` even when N children were reprocessed.

Only callable when the resource is in a terminal state. Returns 409 if
the resource is still in-flight. Returns 404 if the row does not exist.

get.description:
Export validation results for a batch as JSON.

Returns rows with their annotation data.
Use mode=violations (default) for invalid-flagged rows (warnings excluded).
Use mode=remaining for only unactioned (active) violations and warnings.
Use mode=all for every row regardless of annotation status.

parameters.name: mode

schema.description: Export mode: 'all' for every row, 'violations' for invalid-flagged rows (including accepted/dismissed, excluding warnings), or 'remaining' for only unactioned (active) violations and warnings. 'issues' is accepted as a backwards-compatible alias for 'violations'.

FileReprocessResponse.title: FileReprocessResponse
FileReprocessResponse.description:
Response after triggering reprocessing of an existing file.

The same ``file_id`` is returned — the existing row's status is reset to
'uploading' and the Chronos workflow re-runs on the same underlying file.

``reprocessed_count`` and ``attempted_count`` are populated only for the
split-batch path (preinvoice batches whose parent row was deleted after
per-company splitting). Both are ``None`` for single-row reprocess calls.
